name: Effects-only melodic instrument: crackle/noise source → smoothed-random filter → ping-pong feedback delay → spectral harmonic resonator (note, decay, harmonic count, pitch mod) → 'smudge' lo-fi/unison macro → reverb → limiter
goal: Make a playable wind-chime / abstract atmosphere instrument from effects only. Generate vinyl-style crackle (only its density is mapped), or feed any external audio (drums, vocals). Filter it with a resampling-type filter whose cutoff is moved by a sample-and-hold LFO smoothed 100% (random glides), with ~10% drive. Multiply it with a ping-pong delay (6/16, 5/16, down to triplets) at high feedback. Excite a harmonic spectral resonator in note mode, using the granular engine with input quantised, unison 2 and low-damp fixed at 15%. Map fundamental note, decay (blips vs pads), number of harmonics (minimum 6; more = brighter and higher, with high-damp tied to the same macro) and pitch-mod amount (up to 1 semitone) and rate. A 'smudge' macro raises resonator unison spread together with bit/sample-rate reduction (0 = 18 kHz/16-bit, i.e. off). Finish with reverb (size 100, diffusion-network filter on) on time + amount macros, a limiter, macro snapshots and randomisation that excludes note, input level and reverb. Delta vs our click-train comb texture: noise conditioning chain + harmonic resonator macro design.

source.title: Spectral Ambience: Turning Noise into Melodic Synths (Ableton Live 12)
source.transcript_note: Ableton rack build; macro range table was on-screen only (not in transcript), so only spoken values are recorded.

prerequisites: Noise/crackle generator or any audio input
Filter with LFO (S&H + smoothing), ping-pong delay with feedback
Harmonic/spectral resonator (Web Audio: bank of high-Q bandpass filters or comb/modal resonators at harmonics of a note, implementation note)
Bit/sample-rate reducer, reverb, limiter, macro rack

inputs.name: excitation
inputs.description: Crackle/noise (density control) or external audio such as percussion

inputs.name: note
inputs.description: Resonator fundamental (e.g. E0 in the demo)

outputs.name: resonated_atmos
outputs.description: Bell-like wind chimes, plucks or pad-like resonant atmospheres from noise

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
The resonator only sounds when excited; the level macro controls its input/send amount.

The macro min/max range values were shown only in an on-screen screenshot and are not reproduced. Set ranges by ear; spoken values (6 harmonics minimum, ≤1 st pitch mod, 15% low damp, ~10% drive, 18 kHz/16-bit off point) are kept.
Exclude the note, input level and reverb from randomisation so random snapshots stay usable.
Web Audio resonator mapping is an implementation note, not transcript content.

steps.action: Create an effects rack (audio-effect track) with 16 macros. First device: crackle/noise generator; map only its density (crackle level) to a macro. Alternatively route external audio (e.g. bongo drums, vocals) into the rack.
steps.expect: Sparse crackle or the external signal

steps.action: Add a filter in a resampling/character mode, LFO wave sample-and-hold with smoothing 100%, drive ~10%. Map cutoff, LFO amount and LFO rate to macros to sculpt which parts of the noise spectrum excite the resonator.
steps.expect: Noise colour drifts smoothly between random positions

steps.action: Add a ping-pong delay at 100% wet. Map delay time (e.g. 6/16, 5/16, limited down to triplets for ambient use), a small L/R delay offset for stereo interest, and feedback (high).
steps.expect: Crackle multiplied into a denser, stereo stream

steps.action: Add the spectral resonator: note mode, granular engine, quantise input on, unison 2, low damp fixed ~15% (cuts boomy lows). Map fundamental note, decay, number of harmonics (min 6) plus high damp on the same macro, pitch-mod amount (up to 1 st) and rate, and input level.
steps.expect: Pitched bell/chime tones emerge from noise; more harmonics = brighter

steps.action: Add a bit/sample-rate reducer after the resonator. Make one 'smudge' macro that raises the resonator's unison spread, lowers bit depth and lowers sample rate together (0 = 18 kHz/16-bit, i.e. off).
steps.expect: Wider stereo spread with growing lo-fi grit

steps.action: Add reverb (size 100, diffusion-network filter on) and map decay time and dry/wet, then a final limiter to catch peaks.
Play it: short decay for plucks and blips, long decay for pads. Save macro snapshots of good settings and randomise for new territory, with note, input level and reverb excluded from randomisation.
steps.expect: Range from wind chimes to abstract atmospheres

verification: Muting the resonator leaves only filtered/delayed crackle; enabling it produces pitched tones at the set note.
Raising the harmonic count audibly brightens the result.
Randomise never changes the fundamental note.
